unparsed_instruction_finding.question_asked: attempt 1's CONSTANTS verdict was WARN: 47 of 47 instructions consumed, degraded=true, unparsed=1. Which instruction does not parse?
unparsed_instruction_finding.machine_record: reconstruction/evidence/006a2530/evidence.json -> categories.abi_derived.value.observations[obs-0014] = {kind: UNPARSED, raw: "JC 0x006a2561", at: 0x006a2558, reason: "unknown_mnemonic"}, and categories.abi_derived.value.parse = {declared_count: 47, degraded: true, unparsed: 1, flow_complete: false, esp_unresolved: false}
unparsed_instruction_finding.what_it_actually_is: a perfectly well-formed two-byte x86-32 instruction. The bytes at 0x006a2558 are 72 07 (read directly from the image): opcode 0x72 with rel8 0x07, i.e. Jc/Jb -- branch if carry clear, which for an unsigned CMP means 'branch if below'. 0x72 + 7 lands on 0x006a2561, the MOV EAX,EDI clamp. It is the second half of the hit predicate and the reconstruction depends on it: it is the reject when propertyID sorts below the entry's key.
unparsed_instruction_finding.why_the_parser_rejects_it: a grammar gap in the machine tool, not a decoding failure. tools/reconstruction_tooling/abi_infer.py defines BRANCH_MNEM as a literal set that contains the Jcc spellings JA, JAE, JB, JBE, JE, JG, JGE, JL, JLE, JNE, JNO, JNP, JNS, JNZ, JO, JP, JPE, JPO, JS and JZ -- but not the carry aliases JC and JNC. parse_insn() therefore marks the line kind=unparsed with reason=unknown_mnemonic even though JB (the other name for the same opcode) would have matched. tools/** is out of bounds for this worker, so the set was not edited.
unparsed_instruction_finding.effect_on_this_package: the instruction is fully accounted for in the reconstruction (the `propertyID >= found->first` test is exactly its predicate), in this record, and in the source comment at the hit test, which names the opcode 0x72 and the alias. The machine parse record still reports unparsed=1, so CONSTANTS is an expected WARN and is reported as one.
unparsed_instruction_finding.note_on_scope: the same gap would hit any body that uses JC or JNC, including 0x00612db0, whose 0x00612de4 JNC the same grammar would reject. That body is not this target and is not claimed here.

mechanics.shape: pure read; no receiver word is written and no counter is bumped, in contrast to sibling App::PropertyList::AddPropertiesFrom at 0x006a2f10 which INC dword ptr [EBP+0x34] -- the SDK names that word mnOperationsDone
mechanics.lookup: Read the element range at receiver+0x18 and receiver+0x1c, forward the low byte of the word at receiver+0x2c as a fourth argument, and call the shared lower_bound helper 0x00612db0 with mpBegin, mpEnd and &propertyID.
mechanics.helper: 0x00612db0 is cdecl and ends in a bare RET (0x00612dfc). Its element count is the byte distance between the two range pointers divided by the 0x18 stride, computed with IMUL 0x2AAAAAAB / SAR 2 / SHR 0x1F. It then halves: probe at 24*(count>>1), and if that key is strictly below propertyID it advances one element and sets count = count-1-(count>>1), otherwise count = count>>1, looping while count > 0. It returns the first element whose key is >= propertyID, or mpEnd when every key sorts below the request. Verified instruction by instruction against the live 33-instruction listing in this attempt.
mechanics.helper_arity_correction: 0x006a2530 pushes four dwords but 0x00612db0 reads only [ESP+0x08] (mpEnd), [ESP+0x04] (mpBegin, reached through the PUSH ESI at 0x00612db4) and [ESP+0x10] (&propertyID), and never [ESP+0x14]. The fourth push, the low byte of mProperties.mValueCompare, is therefore forwarded and ignored on this path.
mechanics.hit_predicate: found != mpEnd AND propertyID >= found->first, both tests unsigned. 0x006a2552 CMP EAX,EDI / JZ rejects the end sentinel; 0x006a2556 CMP EDX,dword ptr [EAX] followed by the 0x00612db0-style carry branch 0x006a2558 rejects a lower-bound result whose key sorts above the request. The third comparison emitted at 0x006a255a (LEA ECX,[EAX + 0x18] ; CMP EAX,ECX ; JNZ 0x006a2563) is a tautology: an element can never equal itself plus its own size, so the JNZ is always taken and its apparent 'same element' guard is semantically void. The Ghidra rendering of it, 'puVar3 == puVar3 + 6', is a decompiler artefact and carries no meaning.
mechanics.hit_action: *out = &found->second, i.e. the address entry+0x04; return true (AL=1). The four value bytes are NOT copied and the pointer is never dereferenced by this body.
mechanics.miss_with_parent: If mpParent is non-null, load the PARENT's vtable, call slot +0x24 with ECX = parent and (propertyID, out) on the stack, and return the parent's bool unchanged.
mechanics.miss_without_parent: Return false (EAX zeroed). The out pointer is never written on this path, so the caller must not read it unless the call returned true.
mechanics.chain_semantics: The vtable at 0x01408820 stores 0x006A2530 in its own +0x24 slot, which the SDK vtable type also names GetProperty. The escalation port and this function's own vtable slot are therefore the same offset, so a base PropertyList parent re-enters this exact body and the miss path is a walk up the parent chain: the first list in the chain that holds the key answers, and the chain root (mpParent == null) answers false.
mechanics.no_cycle_guard: No depth limit, visited set, or duplicate-receiver test appears in the 47 instructions, so a cyclic parent chain would recurse without bound. Whether any runtime configuration can build one is outside this body.
mechanics.borrowed_pointer_lifetime: Because the published pointer is &found->second, it aliases the receiver's own table storage. Any mutation of that list (SetProperty at +0x14, RemoveProperty at +0x18, Clear at +0x48) can invalidate it. This follows from the address arithmetic, not from any observed caller behaviour.
